subject: Specter-v2: temporary version-hold & tokenizer interop check
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Specter-v2: temporary version-hold & tokenizer interop check

Team —

We ran the Specter-v2 small variant through our intake smoke tests this morning and hit a tokenizer parity failure for edge-case CJK inputs and a KV-cache shape mismatch in runtime that causes incorrect streaming offsets (see attached compat report). The external integration (Nebula) is asking for us to onboard v2-rc3; they also mention a tokenization tweak on their side.

Ask: can Infra/Serving apply a temporary version-hold (prevent auto-rollforward) for specter-v2 variants on hosted and dedicated while we validate the tokenization fixes and confirm the canary plan? Ideally hold the current 2027-05-22 build until we finish the interop checks (targeting EOD 5/24).

Context (short):
- Failure mode: partial tokenization divergence on multi-byte punctuation + KV cache padding mismatch triggers off-by-one on stream positions.
- Risk: customer-facing streaming responses may occasionally truncate or misalign final tokens for ~0.3% of requests on long sequences.
- Immediate mitigation: revert to specter-v1-compatible weights for traffic above 100ms latency; but this increases cost.

I've attached the compat report and tokenizer diff; Priyom, can you confirm whether the cache-shape issue is a model export artifact vs runtime bug? Laura, can you propose a short canary plan if Infra agrees to the hold? Marissa, flag any commercial implications for Nebula's procurement timeline.

Thanks —

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Product Manager, Model Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: specter_v2_compat_report.pdf, tokenizer_diff_specterv2.txt
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Specter-v2: temporary version-hold & tokenizer interop check

Soojin —

Quick read of the artifacts: the KV-cache shape mismatch looks like an export-time padding change in the build pipeline (shape dims off by one in last layer). This is most likely an exporter flag the Nebula team changed (their README says they "enable compact-padding" in rc3). I don't see an immediate runtime allocator bug in our CI traces.

Plan:
1) I can push a validation build to staging that enforces legacy padding semantics (takes ~90m). If that passes tokenization integration tests we'll have higher confidence the issue is export-related.
2) If export is the root cause, a pin on the model version at the control-plane level (prevent auto-rollforward) is sufficient for Hosted/Dedicated until Nebula gives us rc4.
3) If we detect a runtime fallback mismatch, we'll escalate to Serving infra (but low likelihood).

I recommend applying a temporary version-hold while we run the validation build. If Infra can gate auto-rollforward for the specter-v2 family by tag (e.g. tag: specter-v2:20270522-hold) that should be reversible.

I'll start the staging validation now and post results + test diffs to the Drive link.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Applied ML Engineer, Inference Compatibility
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@nebulalabs.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nebulalabs.ai
Date: 2027-05-23T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Specter-v2: temporary version-hold & tokenizer interop check

Thanks for the quick flag, Soojin + team. Apologies — rc3 included an optimization that changed compact-padding semantics for export, and we missed the downstream effects for streaming offsets. We're preparing rc4 which reverts the padding change and includes a small tokenizer mapping table to handle multi-byte punctuation.

We appreciate the hold request. Nebula is fine with a short temporary hold while you run your validation. We can provide a signed build artifact and export flags (link below) and are happy to join a quick triage call if useful.

Artifacts:
- Export flags & notes: https://nebula-artifacts.s3.amazonaws.com/specter/v2/rc4-export.txt
- Weights tarball (signed): https://nebula-artifacts.s3.amazonaws.com/specter/v2/rc4-weights.tgz

Samir Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, Nebula Labs
samir.shah@nebulalabs.ai

Onboarding / procurement: procurement@nebulalabs.ai — our procurement lead is tracking the SLA and the hold window is acceptable as long as it's communicated.
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-24T11:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Specter-v2: temporary version-hold & tokenizer interop check

Confirming status after Priyom's staging validation run:
- Validation run (staging) passed with legacy-padding enforcement; tokenizer diffs reduced to negligible for our canonical prompt set. No streaming offset regressions observed in 10k sample streams.
- Nebula's rc4 export flags (Samir's link) align with our expectations; weights integrity verified.

Request to Infra (action item):
- Apply a temporary control-plane version-hold on the specter-v2:20270522 build across Hosted and Dedicated (prevent auto-rollforward and block any automatic variant swaps).
- Add a canary route: 1% traffic to specter-v2:rc4 on staging-like hardware for 24h, then 10% for 12h, then full if no regressions.
- Expected hold window: 48 hours max (we'll coordinate with Nebula if we need extension).

Commercial note (Marissa): Nebula procurement is aware of the hold and will accept the short delay; no impact to committed SLAs if communicated.

If Infra confirms the hold, I'll draft the customer note and pair with Samir on rollout timing.

Laura Bennett
Program Manager, Model Intake & Safety
Redwood Inference
